verdict_reason: Re-measured the strided protocol head-to-head against the HuggingFace reference on the FULL wikitext-2-raw-v1 test split this round: window 1024 / stride 512 gives HF 25.17045 vs BLME 25.17048 (rel 1.31e-6), 1024/1024 gives 29.94053 vs 29.94052 (rel 1.30e-7), 512/256 gives 28.34971 vs 28.34970 (rel 2.57e-7); BLME's shift-aware denominator counts 287,643 tokens against my transcription's 287,644, i.e. it is off by exactly one over the whole corpus (the first token, which is never predicted) rather than one per window. The crash I reported is FIXED and I verified it directly rather than by inspection: strided_perplexity on a purpose-built GPT2 with n_positions = 128 clamps the pinned 1024 window and returns (52696.07, 10.8723, 8057 tokens, 36035 bytes, 36035 chars) with no exception and no CUDA assert. `logger` is now defined at utils.py:19, so the clamp's warning branch no longer raises NameError.
comparable_reason: Perplexity is the study's scale control and is a near-perfect size proxy by construction (standing measurement: pythia-70m 36.30, distilgpt2 33.41, gpt2 21.80, pythia-160m 21.26, gpt2-medium 16.10, gpt2-large 13.94 -- Spearman -1.00 with n_params over 6 models; bits_per_byte identical). The clamp adds a SECOND comparability break that is now silent: a model with context < 1024 is scored at its own smaller window, and the code's own comment records that window matters by 23% (pythia-70m: 49.09 at 512, 43.15 at 1024, 39.80 at 2048). The warning message literally says 'see _meta_ppl_window' -- and there is no _meta_ppl_window: grepping the whole src/ tree, that string appears exactly once, inside the log line itself. So the one thing that would make a clamped model visibly incomparable is referenced but not emitted. The rare/freq buckets carry the extra tokenizer confound (rare_ids is the bottom 20% of each MODEL'S OWN observed ids); only ppl_rare_over_freq is within-model comparable.
github_reason: No source paper/repo exists for 'perplexity'; the operative reference is the HuggingFace strided sliding-window guide, which the code names. I transcribed that procedure verbatim and ran it head-to-head against strided_perplexity() on gpt2 over the full wikitext-2-raw-v1 test split at three (window, stride) settings this round -- agreement 1.31e-6 / 1.30e-7 / 2.57e-7 relative. Separately verified the clamp against a synthetic 128-context GPT2LMHeadModel.
paper_reason: The protocol reproduces the canonical reference figure exactly: gpt2 / wikitext-2-raw-v1 test / window 1024 / stride 512 = 25.17048 against the HF guide's own 25.17 (rel 1.3e-6). The docstring has been CORRECTED since my last round and is now right: it states 25.17 as the WikiText-2 value, says 21.80 is the default-corpus value, and explicitly retracts the fabricated 'published GPT-2 small number is ~21.8' (the GPT-2 paper reports 29.41). The SHIPPED configuration still reproduces nothing published -- 100 WikiText-103 validation rows, ~13k tokens -- so ppl_overall and bits_per_byte are internally comparable only.
confounds_reason: By design and unchanged: Spearman -1.00 with n_params across six models spanning two families. This is the study's capability floor variable, not beyond-scale structural evidence, and the paper must say so explicitly. Nothing in this round's diff changes that.
defects: The clamp emits no _meta_ key, and its own warning text points at one that does not exist: `f"window -- see _meta_ppl_window."` at utils.py:506 is the ONLY occurrence of that string in src/. A short-context model's ppl_overall is computed at a different window from every other model's, with nothing in the returned dict to say so, and the code's own comment puts that effect at 23%.

No _meta_ key distinguishes the strided value from the per-document fallback either. perplexity.py catches every exception from strided_perplexity and falls back to ppl_overall_perdoc, which on gpt2 is 37.91 against 21.80 -- a 74% difference that is invisible in the output. _meta_ppl_overall_strided and _meta_n_tokens_strided exist but both are _meta_-prefixed, i.e. excluded from the analysis feature matrix, so the feature that IS used carries no protocol flag.

The 'Empty rows are KEPT ... filtering blanks moved ppl 25.17 -> 24.36' rationale (utils.py:464-469) is still dead on the shipped path: cache.py:538 filters `len(row['text']) >= 50` inside load_default_corpus, so zero blank rows ever reach strided_perplexity. The comment describes behaviour the pipeline does not have.

bits_per_byte subtracts len(decode(input_ids[0,:1])) bytes for the unscored first token; for a BOS-prepending tokenizer that first id contributes 0 source bytes, so the subtraction removes bytes that were never in the corpus. Magnitude ~5e-5 relative -- cosmetic, but the stated invariant is false.

The clamp silently changes the stride too, since stride defaults to max_length//2: a 128-context model runs 128/64 rather than 1024/512, compounding the protocol difference the missing _meta_ key hides.
fix: Emit _meta_ppl_window and _meta_ppl_stride with the values actually used, and a _meta_ppl_protocol flag ('strided' vs 'perdoc_fallback') -- the warning text already promises the first of these and it does not exist. Better still, emit the window WITHOUT the _meta_ prefix, or set ppl_overall to NaN when the window had to be clamped, so a short-context model is excluded from a cross-model comparison rather than silently mixed into it. Delete the 'blanks are KEPT' rationale or stop filtering len<50 in load_default_corpus for this task. Guard the byte denominator against a control-token first id (subtract 0 bytes when input_ids[0,0] is in tokenizer.all_special_ids). State in the paper that ppl/bpb is the scale control (Spearman -1.00 with n_params), not beyond-scale evidence.
fix_applied: R25: the clamp's warning referenced _meta_ppl_window, which did not exist anywhere in src/, so a clamped model's ppl_overall was silently on a different protocol (~23%). strided_perplexity now returns the realised window and stride and the task emits both.
